A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CHEEM and retain the four-operation hierarchical exploration-exploitation framework. Despite substantial revisions, their readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original CHEEM experiments on VDD and 5-Datasets, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, and task-order studies.

after.justification: v5 reports original MTIL and VDD experiments, including different backbones, task-ID recognition, search sensitivities, and classifier-head analyses.

M1.justification: The HEE core remains, but v5 replaces the MLP Adapt operation with LoRA, introduces MLPDown as the primary memory placement alongside attention projection, and changes architecture selection from best validation accuracy to a compute-sensitive search (Sections 3.2–3.4). It also adds centroid-based task-ID inference and a lightweight recognition variant, replacing v4's reliance on supplied task IDs.

E1.justification: Evaluation changes from task-incremental learning with known task IDs to class-incremental learning with unknown test-time task IDs. MTIL adds coverage including Caltech101, EuroSAT, Food101, Oxford Pets, Stanford Cars, and SUN397. The 5-Datasets evaluation disappears: CIFAR10, Fashion-MNIST, and not-MNIST are removed, while MNIST and SVHN remain through MTIL and VDD respectively.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set is substantially replaced. v5 retains EWC, L2P, and S-Prompts, adds CODA-Prompt, DualPrompt, DIKI, LoRA-CL, MoAL, Tuna, and full/LoRA fine-tuning references, and adds MoEAdapter4CL in Appendix G. v4's L2G variants, L2 regularization, experience replay, SupSup, EFT, and Lightweight Learner comparisons are absent.

E3.justification: v4 uses ViT-B/8 at 72×72; v5 uses 224×224 inputs with ViT-B/16, DEiT-Tiny/16, and additional CLIP experiments. Appendix H reconstructs VDD using original images and revised splits where available, specifies no augmentation, and changes the stated VDD supernet/fine-tuning budgets from 100/30 to 50/20 epochs. Accuracy and forgetting now exclude the ImageNet base task, and FoM is introduced.

E4.justification: v5 adds exploration-probability and compute-tolerance sweeps, lightweight task-recognition studies, CLIP generalization tests, and local-versus-global classifier-head analysis (Figure 10; Appendices F, G, I). Placement, HEE-versus-uniform sampling, and task-order questions receive revised experiments. v4's shortcut, prompt-length, and training-duration ablations are removed. The original component-identification analysis is largely retained in Appendix J.

E5.justification: Principal comparisons retain three-seed mean and ± reporting. However, v4 Table 13 reports task-order results averaged over three seeds with uncertainty values, whereas v5 Table 10 provides order-specific point estimates without seed counts or uncertainties. This is a limited reporting change; it does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Most benchmark results are replaced or newly reported. For example, v4 Table 2 reports VDD accuracy of 83.44 ± 0.50, while v5 Table 12 reports 86.71 ± 0.23 for default CHEEM under changed conditions; these are not a same-setting performance gain. MTIL accuracy of 85.88 ± 0.29 and extensive forgetting, compute, and routing results are added. The eleven component scores from v4 Table 1 remain in v5 Table 20, but its frozen-backbone classifier row is removed.

T1.justification: v5 adds Appendix I's formal local/global argmax setup, Gaussian-logit assumptions, and derivations of agreement probabilities involving competing out-of-task classes. It also introduces the mathematical FoM definition in Equation 6. These extend substantially beyond v4's method and evaluation equations; the retained ViT and HEE equations are not new theory.

C1.justification: The main contribution changes from task-incremental learning through attention-projection memory to an exemplar-free class-incremental framework with internal parameter memory and external task-centroid memory. v5 emphasizes task-adaptive computation, FoM superiority, and approaching fine-tuning references on MTIL/VDD, replacing v4's projection-layer identification and first-ViT-on-VDD contribution framing.

C2.justification: v4's known-task-ID limitation and proposed future inference solution are replaced by evaluated routing-accuracy/compute tradeoffs in v5 Appendix G. v5 newly attributes poor baseline performance to local/global classifier-head mismatch and interprets architecture differences through backbone capacity. HEE's benefit is reframed around parameter economy when accuracy is comparable to uniform sampling, rather than v4's large accuracy advantage.

D1.justification: v5 adds a concrete project repository address, per-stage training times (Table 7), and documentation of revised checkpoints and dataset reconstruction (Appendix H). It does not retain v4's detailed batch sizes, evolutionary-search population and iteration settings, regularization recipe, or baseline-porting instructions from Appendices B–C and F. Reproducibility information is substantially revised, with both additions and losses.

R1.justification: v5 substantially repositions CHEEM around class-incremental head design, task-dependent computation, and parameter-efficient adaptation. It adds discussion or citations covering LoRA, InfLoRA, SD-LoRA, DIKI, MoAL, Tuna, and mixture-of-experts adapters, while removing the broad replay/generative-replay survey. S-Prompts becomes the acknowledged source of external task-centroid memory, rather than primarily a comparator and prospective extension.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The introduction adopts four organizing questions, related work moves before the method, and the original component-identification section moves to Appendix J. The appendices are reorganized around the revised experiments and new analyses.

P2.justification: v5 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws the method taxonomy and memory diagrams, and depicts learned architectures using separate attention and MLP blocks. Results are reorganized into backbone-grouped accuracy/forgetting/FLOPs tables, with new FoM displays and sensitivity plots. Numerous earlier architecture visualizations disappear, while the retained component-selection table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses v4 Section 3.3's central applicability limitation by implementing and evaluating inference without supplied task IDs. Controlled LoRA-CL comparisons, classifier-head diagnostics, and measured recognition/training costs substantially strengthen evidence about the method's mechanisms and practical tradeoffs. These gains outweigh the loss of some implementation detail and older ablations. The improvement does not depend on comparing incompatible accuracy scores or accepting the very large FoM ratios, which are amplified by a near-zero fine-tuning gap.
